about: The Eastertide Introit for the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: All the wealthy among the people will seek your favor. Virgins will be brought to the King, following her; her closest companions will be brought to you with joy and exultation. Alleluia, alleluia. My heart has poured forth a noble word; I recite my works to the King. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen. All the wealthy among the people will seek your favor. Virgins will be brought to the King, following her; her closest companions will be brought to you with joy and exultation. Alleluia, alleluia.

ex.w001: The Latin speaks of entreating someone’s face: seeking that person’s favor.
ex.w012: These are the woman’s closest companions, following her to the King.
ex.w015: The psalm addresses more than one person. This “you” is not automatically the person addressed in the opening line.
ex.w022: Here the heart pours forth words: the verb describes speech.
ex.w029: “Works” is read here as the poet’s compositions, recited to the King.
